text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Newfoundland school reform halted: Churches rejoice over court's approval of injunction to stop closings.
- Democracy watered down in Hong Kong: Proposed changes to political map push opposition parties to fringe.
- Germany big winner in NATO: Expansion means country will be surrounded by allies.
- U.S. Senate probes China-Clinton link: Former fund raiser offers to co-operate.
- More boys physically abused than girls: Ontario survey also indicates one in eight girls and one in 23 boys suffer sexual abuse.
- Baillie was asked to resign: Former chief of financial services task force contradicts government contention that decision was mutual.
- IPL and Noverco strike huge deal: Calgary company to pay C$330 million for stake in Gaz Metro parent and become Hydro-Quebec's ally.
- K mart Canada grabs merchandiser from Eaton's ranks: suggests new owners aim for revival.
- Magna wins key GM contract: Parts firm to manage development of Cadillac Catera interior.
- IPL in C$330 million Quebec deal: The Alberta pipeline buys into gas distributor that serves Eastern Canada and is 41 percent held by Hydro-Quebec.
- Modest price rally fails to dust off gold's dull image.
- Spar joins two teams seeking C$600 million helicopter contract.
